nodes.summary: For `Q ∈ ℝ`, `cqrBand q_lo q_hi Q x = [q_lo x - Q, q_hi x + Q]`.
nodes.title: The CQR band for a finite threshold is an interval

nodes.summary: For a threshold `Q ∈ ℝ ∪ {+∞}`, the band at `x` is `[q_lo x - Q, q_hi x + Q]`, written as the set of `y` with `q_lo x - y ≤ Q` and `y - q_hi x ≤ Q`; it is all of `ℝ` when `Q = ⊤`.
nodes.title: CQR prediction band

nodes.summary: For fitted lower and upper conditional quantile functions `q_lo`, `q_hi`, the score of a data point `(x, y)` is `max (q_lo x - y) (y - q_hi x)`: negative when `y` lies strictly inside `[q_lo x, q_hi x]`, and the signed distance to the nearer endpoint otherwise.
nodes.title: CQR conformity score

nodes.summary: The `k`-th smallest CQR score of the calibration points `Z i.castSucc` (counted with multiplicity), and `⊤` when `k > n`. With `k = ⌈(1 - α)(n + 1)⌉` this is the `(1 - α)(1 + 1/n)`-th empirical quantile `Q_{1-α}(E, I₂)` of Romano, Patterson and Candès (NeurIPS 2019, arXiv:1905.03222, Algorithm 1), with `Q = +∞` when that level exceeds `1`.
nodes.title: CQR threshold

nodes.summary: Under the hypotheses of the lower bound, if moreover the `n + 1` CQR scores are almost surely distinct, the test response lies in the CQR band with probability at most `1 - α + 1 / (n + 1)`.
nodes.title: CQR coverage (upper bound without ties)

nodes.summary: `y` lies in the band at `x` with threshold `Q` iff the CQR score of `(x, y)` is at most `Q`.
nodes.title: Membership in the CQR band through the score

nodes.summary: Let the law `μ` of the data `Z : Fin (n + 1) → 𝒳 × ℝ` (`n` calibration points, then the test point) be a probability measure invariant under every coordinate permutation, and let `q_lo`, `q_hi` be measurable. For `0 ≤ α < 1`, with `k = ⌈(1 - α)(n + 1)⌉`, the test response lies in the CQR band at the test covariate with probability at least `1 - α`.
nodes.title: CQR coverage (lower bound)

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
